subject.title: [Bug]: API keys can leak in error messages when a custom provider's base URL is unreachable

question: Should this credential-exposure report be handled as a security-sensitive shared provider error-boundary fix before any automated repair is queued?
rationale: The source evidence shows a real raw-error boundary gap, but credential redaction and provider transport coverage need maintainer/security ownership before deciding the exact fix scope.

options.title: Sponsor shared sanitization fix
options.body: Treat the report as security-sensitive and fix the shared provider/network error boundary plus package-provider coverage with regression tests.

options.title: Narrow to proven OpenAI paths first
options.body: Require a live or mocked custom-provider repro and patch only the confirmed OpenAI Responses/Completions paths before broader redaction work.

options.title: Hold for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures a concrete unreachable-endpoint failure showing the leaked value.

recommendation.title: Sponsor shared sanitization fix
recommendation.body: Treat the report as security-sensitive and fix the shared provider/network error boundary plus package-provider coverage with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent refactor ownership place the active provider transport implementation under this area history.
